skill.name: writing-shape
skill.description: Turn fixed raw material into a coherent article through an interactive, paragraph-by-paragraph writing process.
skill.summary: Shape notes, fragments, or transcripts into a structured article with deliberate grounding and format choices.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by prose and Markdown syntax. The skill contains no command execution, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or other semantic security concern.

static_findings.snippet: - **Inline vs. callout.** Tips, warnings, and asides go in callouts (`> [!TIP]`, `> [!NOTE]`) — but
If the user did not say where to save the article, ask once and remember the path.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 64 uses Markdown inline code to show callout syntax. It contains no Ruby, shell execution, or executable command instructions.
Line 13 asks the user to provide an article output path. It does not inspect the system or discover environment details.

content.user_title: Shape Raw Notes into a Coherent Article
content.value_statement: Raw notes and transcripts rarely provide a clear path for readers. This skill guides an interactive, paragraph-by-paragraph process that builds a coherent article.
actual_capabilities: Reads a complete Markdown source before proposing an article structure.
Establishes the concepts that the intended reader already understands.
Drafts two or three openings with different theses or angles.
Builds the article one agreed paragraph or content block at a time.
Tracks grounded concepts and identifies missing foundations before using them.
Compares prose, lists, tables, callouts, quotes, and code formatting for each block.
limitations: Requires a fixed Markdown file containing the available source material.
Does not research new facts or invent missing examples.
Does not edit the raw material file.
Does not publish articles or optimize them for a specific platform.

use_cases.title: Turn Research Notes into an Essay
use_cases.description: Develop a clear thesis and sequence from collected notes while preserving the writer's decisions.

use_cases.title: Convert Interviews into Articles
use_cases.description: Shape transcript material into a readable article with deliberate quotation and paraphrase choices.

use_cases.title: Build Technical Explanations
use_cases.description: Order concepts so readers receive each required foundation before later sections depend on it.

prompt_templates.title: Shape a Basic Article
prompt_templates.prompt: Shape the raw material in [input path] into an article saved at [output path]. Start by asking me about the intended reader.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you have notes and want guided help creating an article.

prompt_templates.title: Develop Openings for an Audience
prompt_templates.prompt: Read [input path] fully. The audience is [audience], and they already understand [prerequisites]. Propose three openings with distinct arguments before drafting further.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the audience is known but the article angle is unsettled.

prompt_templates.title: Shape a Transcript
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn the transcript in [input path] into [output path]. Preserve exact wording only when it matters, and discuss each quote or paraphrase choice with me.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when converting an interview or conversation into an article.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Rigorous Grounding Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Shape [input path] into [output path] for [audience]. Track grounded concepts after every block, challenge weak transitions, and identify source gaps before continuing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced articles where conceptual order and argumentative continuity are critical.

output_examples.input: Notes about slow customer onboarding for an audience of product managers.
output: Opening A: Most onboarding delays begin before a customer sees the product.
Opening B: Faster onboarding depends less on fewer steps than on clearer decisions.
Opening C: Teams measure onboarding time, but often ignore onboarding uncertainty.

output_examples.input: The next paragraph discusses activation metrics, but the audience only knows basic analytics.
output_examples.output: Activation metrics are not grounded yet. Add a short definition and example before the paragraph depends on that concept.

output_examples.input: Three repeated product examples each contain a problem, intervention, and result.
output_examples.output: Use a table because the same three fields repeat across every example. Keep any interpretation in prose after the table.

best_practices: Provide one complete Markdown source file and a separate output path.
Define the intended reader and their existing knowledge before choosing an opening.
Review each proposed block and edit the output file between turns when needed.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to research facts that are absent from the source.
Do not use the raw material file as the article output.
Do not approve several blocks at once when paragraph-level review matters.

faq.question: What source formats does this skill accept?
faq.answer: It expects a Markdown file containing notes, fragments, prose, or a transcript.

faq.question: Does it change my source file?
faq.answer: No. The source remains read-only, and the skill writes the article to a separate path.

faq.question: Can it research missing information?
faq.answer: No. It identifies gaps and asks you to supply material or remove the unsupported section.

faq.question: How does it choose an article structure?
faq.answer: It proposes different openings, follows the selected argument, and adds each required concept before later sections use it.

faq.question: Can I edit the article during the session?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill rereads the output before each write so it can preserve your changes.

faq.question: Does it publish the finished article?
faq.answer: No. Publishing, platform formatting, and unrequested frontmatter are outside its scope.
